statements.status_notes: CVE-2016-9114 is a NULL pointer dereference in the opj_decompress PNM writer (imagetopnm, convert.c:1943 in OpenJPEG 2.1.2): a component data buffer left NULL by the decoder is read. It is a denial of service in the command-line tool when a crafted file is decoded, reported as https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/issues/857, where the reporter confirmed the PoC no longer crashes on later upstream code. Ubuntu attributes the fix to upstream changes released in 2.2.0 (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/2fa0fc61f2d546c8b67e7c5a9cbc61d98e1f7af0 and https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/784d4d47e97b5d0fccccbd931349997a0e2074cc) and lists 18.04 and later as not affected: https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2016-9114. Debian's tracker rates it unimportant and records no fixed version. This package builds OpenJPEG 2.5.3. Checked in the shipped 2.5.3 source, two guards close this path: imagetopnm in src/bin/jp2/convert.c aborts with 'planes[n] == NULL' before reading the red, green or blue plane when its data pointer is NULL, and opj_j2k_are_all_used_components_decoded() in src/lib/openjp2/j2k.c fails the decode when any requested component has no data (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/b2751967ecabf8d8856e85ab91e25d4f235e2eb3, released in 2.4.0), so opj_decompress stops before any writer runs.
